speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These include Ms Tin Pei Ling1, Mr Gerald Giam2,3, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim4, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim5, Ms Hazel Poa6, Mr Darryl David7, Mr Desmond Choo8, Dr Shahira Abdullah9,10,11,12,13, Ms He Ting Ru14 and Mr Yip Hon Weng15.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, I will speak on the incident that has weighed heavily on our minds and our hearts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: No amount of words can describe our shock and grief.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On behalf of the Ministry of Education (MOE), we would like to express our deepest condolences to the family for their immeasurable loss.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our thoughts are also with the staff and students of River Valley High School.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE has and will continue to provide all possible support to the school community, including the affected families.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are also closely monitoring the well-being of the students in River Valley High School and beyond River Valley High School.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Since the incident, many people, including several Members of this House, have stepped forward to offer their assistance in one way or another.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On behalf of the school and our education fraternity, I would like to express our deep gratitude to hon Members of the House and the larger community for your support, encouragement and prayers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I would also like to thank the mainstream media for exercising sensitivity in reporting this incident.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They did so, out of respect for the families involved and to avoid further traumatising other students and staff.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will share with the House a chronological account of the facts of the incident and describe the support that we are providing to the staff and students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I seek Members’ understanding that there are certain aspects of the incident that I cannot discuss as the matter is before the Courts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will also explain what MOE is doing to ensure the well-being and safety of our wider school community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The students returned to their classroom immediately and called their teacher.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Subsequently, the 16-year-old student made the same request to another group of students in the classroom next to the said toilet.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The students’ immediate response was to apply the emergency "Run-Hide-Tell" lockdown drill.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They went into their classroom, locked the doors from within and quickly called their Form Teachers for help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A teacher who first arrived at the scene instructed the 16-year-old student to put down the axe.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: He was then escorted away to a meeting room.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Thereafter, other teachers called the Police and checked the toilet where the 16-year-old was found outside.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Police officers and Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) paramedics despatched to the scene found a 13-year-old student lying motionless in the said toilet with multiple wounds.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: He has since been in remand for psychiatric assessment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Once the situation was under control, the Principal broke the news to the rest of her staff, before speaking to the students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: She shared that a serious incident had happened and asked all students to contact their parents to assure them that they were safe.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Soon after, the Principal separately spoke to the group of students who were most affected by the incident.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Other teachers also came together to support and render assistance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For students who assisted the Police with the interviews, parental consent was duly sought and every student was accompanied by a teacher throughout the entire process.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Other parents were also informed via Parents Gateway that a serious incident had happened in school, so they could look out for their children once they were dismissed for the day.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: From 3.15 pm, students were progressively dismissed, with teachers stationed at various gates to give students and parents assurance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: By the same evening, parents were informed that a member of the RV family had passed away.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The school advised parents to monitor the well-being of their child.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Parents who were worried for their child’s well-being were encouraged to contact their Form Teachers to work out ways to support their children both at home and in school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On Tuesday, 20 July, we set up a “Caring Actions in Response to an Emergency” or CARE Post at RV to provide psychological support to students and staff who needed immediate help, though it was a non-school day.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Together, they reached out to affected teachers and students, who were encouraged to walk in any time they needed someone to talk to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We know this incident has had a profound impact beyond River Valley High School.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Together with my senior colleagues at MOE, I met with 350 Principals from Primary schools to Junior Colleges on 20 July, Hari Raya Haji.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We discussed the situation with them and shared with them the resources they could tap on to identify students and staff who may display signs of distress so that they can be encouraged to seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When school resumed on the morning of Wednesday, 21 July, River Valley High School teachers, supported by MOE CARE officers and counsellors, conducted check-in sessions with students to provide them with a safe place to share their thoughts and feelings.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers called those who were not in school to check on how they were doing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students and teachers who needed time-off were granted leave.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Master teachers from MOE were deployed to take over some classes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where needed, students and staff will be referred to healthcare agencies for professional assistance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Most heartening, within the school community, the students initiated their own small acts of kindness.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some distributed small gifts and snack packs; others sent encouraging notes and sweet treats.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students are looking out not just for themselves, but also their teachers and urging them to seek help where needed.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The School Advisory Committee, Parent-Teacher Association, parents and alumni as well as counsellors from social service agencies and community have also rallied around River Valley High School.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This includes the counsellors on standby from Boon Lay.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All these speak volumes of the compassion and strength of the River Valley High School community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have received many constructive suggestions, questions and feedback in the wake of this tragedy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They fall largely into two groups: mental health and the security of our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some students impose high expectations on themselves, while others have parents who place high expectations on them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some students also have difficulty coping with the rigours of our education system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Over and above dealing with the problems of adolescence, they are all learning to cope with the pressures of a competitive, high-performing environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Previous generations also faced their own considerable challenges, including poverty and war.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But perhaps for our youths growing up in today’s complex and fast-paced world, their challenges are intensified by what happens online, where comparisons are incessant and unrelenting, adding yet another layer of social pressure.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why, as a society, we must continuously improve and strengthen our support system to better prepare our children to not only withstand the pressures they face but also thrive despite these pressures.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We cannot shield our children from pressures entirely, any more than we can shield them from the common challenges of adolescence.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But we must do all we can to help our children find themselves and find their footing in an intense environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our approach should not only be to strengthen the overall system of support, but to engender a much more caring, much more nurturing environment in our society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will share some of our support measures from upstream prevention, to the identification of and the intervention for those at risk.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It includes enhanced features on Mental Health Education, designed to develop our students’ mental health literacy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, they learn to differentiate normal stress from distress and mental illness, so that they can seek help before becoming overwhelmed.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These CCE lessons also teach them to break negative thinking patterns, overcome social emotional problems, seek help when they need to and manage their emotions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students are also taught how to actively stand up against stigma around mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Peer support is another crucial pillar in our efforts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our hope is for all students to learn to sit with a friend who is distressed, show empathy and care and encourage him or her to seek help from trusted adults like parents, teachers or counsellors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Every school has a support network for our students in need.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Beyond equipping our students with the basic coping mechanisms, our teachers keep a watchful eye over their students and provide a listening ear.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If they notice something amiss, teachers reach out and guide our students to work on their difficulties as they are trained with basic counselling skills.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students also have access to another group of teachers called the teacher counsellors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is a special group of teachers who have received additional training so that they can help students who are dealing with more challenging social-emotional problems, such as grief and loss.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When students need additional support, they can see the school counsellor.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And school counsellors are specialised personnel who provide dedicated counselling support.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This support network works most effectively when the partnership with the family is strong.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: COVID-19 has compounded the challenges our young people face.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Much of their usual social support networks and routines have been disrupted, leading to prolonged periods of uncertainty, anxiety and loneliness for many.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: COVID-19 safe management measures were implemented in schools so that our children can be physically in schools with their teachers and classmates for as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, however, we have had to suspend many interactive and community activities, like Co-Curricular Activities (CCAs), National School Games, Cohort Camps and Learning Journeys.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We want to create more time and space for students to pursue experiences that broaden their emotional and psychological horizons and strengthen their resilience.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To this end, we want to work with parents and community groups to establish a caring and enabling society that gives greater attention to the well-being of our young.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, we will strengthen the support network in our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is an increase from the over 700 teacher counsellors we have currently deployed in schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All schools now have at least one school counsellor, while some have two.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where feasible, we will recruit more school counsellors or re-role suitable educators to augment the counselling support network.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are currently putting our plans together on how CCAs can be conducted safely within national safe management measures.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will also dedicate more time and attention to checking in on the well-being of our students regularly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Schools currently have orientation programmes for new students at the start of every school year.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Henceforth, teachers will devote time at the start of every school term to check in on the well-being of their students and guide them to know how, where and when to get help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Last month, we had announced the removal of the CLTs for the 2021 Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE).

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While these topics would have already been taught in schools, removing them from the national examinations would help to relieve the revision load and examination stress for our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are taking a whole-of-Government approach to address these issues.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOH and MSF have set up a new inter-agency task force, which transited from the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Task Force.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chaired by Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, this task force brings together the capabilities and capacities of different agencies to develop an overarching national strategy and action plan on mental health and well-being.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As a member of this task force, MOE will work with MOH and MSF to give focus to the youth segment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This tragic incident could have happened outside of school as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will, therefore, need a whole-of-society effort to keep our children, families and community safe to avoid such a tragic incident from happening again.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We need a communal safety net, underpinned by a caring and nurturing culture, for all our people, especially our youths, so that, collectively, we send them the unequivocal message that no one will ever be alone and no one needs to be going through life's toughest moment alone.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I am encouraged to see that community efforts have already been gaining momentum.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Since February 2020, people from all walks of life have contributed to the Youth Mental Well-being Network.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They have identified gaps around them that they would like to address and are currently developing ground-up solutions to improve youth mental well-being.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These projects include creating programmes to enhance emotional resilience, bringing inspirational stories of hope to our youth and increasing parents' emotional literacy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Since last Monday, the public outpourings of care and support have been overwhelming.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are deeply grateful that so many people want to help ease the pain of the RV family.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, I encourage all of us to look within our own social circles and start from here.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As parents, we all want what is best for our children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As they learn to navigate and face tomorrow's challenges on their own, it is not easy to know when to nudge them, when to stretch them, when to help them, or when to let go.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Within our own families, we can all spend a bit more time listening to our children's thoughts and feelings.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let them share with us what they find stressful.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Give them the space to process their emotions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us walk alongside them as they grow and learn to handle their new challenges.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We can have more frank conversations with our children and families on the definition of success.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As a parent myself, I have come to realise that success must be defined by helping my children to realise their own potential, develop their own strengths and, ultimately, be confident in themselves.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Success cannot, should not and must not be the constant need to be compared with someone else and having to live up to somebody else's image.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The greatest gift that we can give our children is to accept and love them unconditionally and help them be at ease with who they are.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As parents, the greatest assurance that we can give our children is to affirm them and give them the confidence to find their own ways.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Do our actions and choice of words build people up or tear people down?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As adults, let us set the right tone and example.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us work together to break the vicious cycles of negativity by standing up for others and responding with grace and compassion.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We can stop toxic conversations online and amplify messages of strength, care and positivity through our online networks instead.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All of us can be kind to each other.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All of us can look out for one another, no matter how tough the competition might be or how intense the pressures can be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To the students and teachers who visited our CARE Post at River Valley High School, I know it took courage for you to step forward and seek help, and I encourage you to continue doing so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To those who are struggling still, I want you to know that we are here for you.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us know if you need help and we will do what we can to support you.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I appeal to everyone not to stigmatise those who come forward to seek help – be they students, staff, parents or families.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Reaching out for help is a sign of strength and not weakness.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let this incident motivate all of us to take down our barriers and treat struggling individuals who step forward with care and compassion.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have discussed this issue with school leaders and they were unanimous in their responses.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: School is like a second home to our children and all of us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is a safe place where values are cultivated, lifelong relationships built and a shared identity forged.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is a warm and supportive environment that allows students with different learning needs and aspirations to discover their passions and develop their strengths.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, schools are secured with physical barriers, such as fences, roller shutters, CCTVs and alarm systems, that can trigger an alert in the event of an intrusion.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Security officers also conduct spot checks and register visitors before entry into the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All schools have a School Emergency Structure to deal with emergencies, to respond, recover and restore the situation back to normalcy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They cover areas, such as first aid, search, trauma management, evacuation, handling of casualties and managing the emergency operations centre.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teachers are trained to respond to different emergency scenarios.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: School leaders, staff and students take part in regular emergency training exercises to practise how to handle emergency situations in the school, including security incidents.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Police and SCDF are involved in such training exercises and drills which are part of the wider community safety net.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In our efforts to enhance security at our schools, we do not want to compromise the quality of school experience for our staff and students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have asked myself this difficult question: what would it feel like if I must empty my pockets, be frisked and have my bag checked before stepping through my house door or school gate?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Also, how would my fellow family members and students feel?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How would we relate to one another in such an environment?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Or will it create in me a siege mentality?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: None of us wish to return to a home with metal scanners and bag checks.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I can understand that parents are understandably worried.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The security and well-being of our students and staff are critical and schools must continue to be safe places for students to learn, grow and play.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The real key to staying safe lies not with more intrusive security measures, but in prevention and enhanced community vigilance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We all have a collective role to play in looking out for potentially deviant or worrying behaviours and report possible threats in our midst.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not want to turn our schools into fortresses, which will create unease and stress amongst our staff and students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We also do not wish to paradoxically engender a siege mentality amongst students and staff, causing them to take extreme measures to protect themselves, at the expense of a shared sense of security.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: (In Mandarin):    In the wake of the tragic incident at River Valley High School, the Principal, teachers and students of the school have remained stoic; and parents and members of the public readily came forward to express their care and support.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As our nation grieves, we have been reflecting on how to prevent similar tragedies from happening again.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At present, all teachers are trained in basic counselling skills and are able to offer counselling support to students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students also have access to another group of teachers called the teacher counsellors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is a special group of teachers who have received additional training so that they can help students who are dealing with more challenging social-emotional problems.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is important for us parents to form strong partnerships with the schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As a parent, I fully understand the care and aspirations that we have for our children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We should spend more time listening to how they feel and helping them to realise their own potential.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I also often remind myself of the importance of cultivating our children’s innate sense of confidence and not comparing them to others.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is because our sense of self-worth should not be defined relative to others.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As a society, we need a communal safety net, underpinned by a caring and nurturing culture.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must not stigmatise those who come forward to seek help, be they students or families.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must set positive examples and do our part in contributing to a warm and inclusive environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As a parent, I can understand the worries and concerns surrounding security in schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our schools are like a second home for our children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is a place for them to learn, grow and have fun together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In our efforts to enhance security at our schools, we have to ensure that they remain trusted shared spaces.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Following this tragic incident, the alumni, students, parents and members of the public, have shown tremendous care and empathy towards the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On behalf of River Valley High School, I would like to express my appreciation to all of you.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: During this period, we have also seen how the teachers, students and alumni of the school have stood in solidarity through adversity.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: May River Valley High School remain ever resilient and grow even stronger as they overcome this tragedy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: (In English):  Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, let me conclude in English.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I visited River Valley High School on the day of the incident and spoke with the leaders, teachers, staff and some students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To the students of River Valley High School, thank you for showing care and compassion to one another.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To the teachers, despite your own grief and shock, you attended to your students and are still helping them to cope with their difficult emotions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To the Principal, who was on medical leave, thank you for rushing back to the school to personally handle the incident.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I know how painful it is for you, but I know how you have kept this to yourself while putting your students, teachers and staff's interests before all else.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All of us, especially as parents, are appreciative of the leadership and compassion shown by the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It gives us confidence that our children are in good hands.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To all principals, teachers and school counsellors across the entire nation who have been looking out for our students in their own schools, thank you for your dedication, commitment and care.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: May we stand united in this effort and be vigilant as we heal as a community and as a nation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: My children, your children, our children, our future.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: And I have also spent considerable time with the staff and students in River Valley High School in my last five years as the Member of Parliament for Boon Lay constituency.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: My heart really goes out to the affected families as well as the staff and the students.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: As what the Minister has mentioned earlier, the response by the River Valley High School community in the face of this adversity has been commendable.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: In the face of this tragic incident, teachers, school leaders, staff, including parents and alumni, deserve our full support and encouragement.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I have a few questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our preliminary sense was that the students have applied their drills as they were taught, they maintained their composure, locked themselves in their classroom and sought help immediately.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To the teachers who responded to the incident, I must say that I was very touched by how they calmly led away the 16-year-old, while protecting the rest of the children in the events that unfolded.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there are many positives that I think we can take away from this incident, despite the tragedy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The consensus amongst the professional colleagues was that we should try to let the school come together, take stock of the situation and support one another, rather than to let individuals grieve alone in their homes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the last few days, we have seen positive responses from the River Valley High School community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We were encouraged to see both students and staff progressively regaining the daily rhythm of their school life and it is a healthy sign.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, we know that the implications from this particular incident may still take some time to unfold.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why, be it in River Valley High School or beyond River Valley High School, we have asked all our staff, teachers and principals to take extra precaution to be more alert to those individuals who might be distressed and need additional help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the second issue, yes, MOE, to the extent possible, within the ambit of the medical-in-confidence rules, we work closely with MHA and MOH, particularly, if there is a threat that the person in distress might pose to the community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We want to encourage people to come forward and seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not want people to put off seeking help because they think that they might be stigmatised or that their medical records will be shared with other agencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is why we will always respect the medical-in-confidence record of the students and staff unless they agree to pass it over to us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, in situations – and that has happened before, including in recent weeks – where if the agencies from MHA to MOH make an assessment that a particular distressed individual might be of harm to the wider community, then we would work with the community partners to manage the situation together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But having said that, we are fully cognisant that for distressed individuals, coming forward to seek help may not be something that they may be comfortable with or know how to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, beyond those who come forward to seek help, we are constantly on the lookout for people who might be troubled but do not come forward to seek help, maybe because they fear being stigmatised or they fear that they will not be accepted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is why we want to send out a message to everyone that if you need help, come forward.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us, as a community, embrace them with care and compassion, so that they need not fear that they will be stigmatised or rejected by us.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have a question for the Minister on school security in general.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am aware that many schools hire an Operations Manager, who is usually someone with military or law enforcement experience.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And certainly, I think we can see that this is helpful if the school has to manage any security or other incidents.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether this is a baseline requirement for all schools, that they need to have an Operations Manager with such experience.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As to whether it is a prerequisite for them to be trained previously in the security agencies, be it the SAF or MHA, that would be useful, but it is not a prerequisite because there are also other operational managers that bring with them security experiences, organisational experiences, beyond the SAF and MHA.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The incident has hit many of us hard.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: As a parent, I share the sadness, the fear and the disappointment.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We are not just the curators of knowledge, the choreographers of behaviour.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We are not just disciplinarians, we are their friend, we are their confidant.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: When things go south, it is very easy to pinpoint the teachers and the staff.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For the past week, thoughts of doubts, what ifs, maybes, have filled many of our heads, but, fundamentally and rationally, I know that schools must remain a safe space.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And, fundamentally, are our teachers prepared for major incidents?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How else can we strengthen our school security so that schools remain a safe space for all?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Inevitably, mental health is the talk of the town.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My worry is that this talk will equate to fear and resets our efforts in destigmatising mental health.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, it is not easy to be a teacher.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, the role of a teacher goes beyond just imparting knowledge to our younger generation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They take on many responsibilities, including the guidance of our children in their social-emotional development, in their career choices and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In my short time in MOE, I have seen the determination in our teachers to want to do the best for the children under their charge, no matter how hard it might be or how tough or how varied the challenges might be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How to lock down the schools, how to keep the boundaries of the school safe, how to shutter down to have safe spaces for our students and staff such that we can buy time until reinforcement or the security forces arrive.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, in the response to this particular incident, I think the students and teachers all showed the presence of mind to be able to apply their drills, albeit learnt for a different scenario, into this scenario to safeguard one another.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I think we will need to continue to have a variety of scenarios to alert our security managers, students and staff to the range of threats that might happen.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Despite that range of threats, some of the basic fundamental drills, the principles behind the drills, are applicable.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that has been demonstrated in this particular incident.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, teachers and staff do get posted and rostered to different schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At any point in time, the schools have a responsibility to make sure that they have an intact incident management team and they have sufficient trained people to execute the drills with the students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because of the posting cycle, in the event there is a shortfall, we will quickly remedy that by making sure that the necessary people are trained to execute the actions accordingly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the second point, it is something that concerns us as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have asked ourselves, that through this incident, will our wider community, instead of embracing and helping those in distress, end up rejecting them, ostracising them or stigmatising them?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why today, I want to make an appeal to everyone to not do this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: To be able to step forward to seek help is not a sign of weakness.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It takes courage to step forward and seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us help those people in distress in our own ways by, first, not stigmatising them, but by accepting them as part of our community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Maybe, very importantly for us to remember, is that the mental distress that some members of our community go through can happen to anyone of us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is why we need to be conscious that this can happen to anyone and, therefore, we need to adopt a collective attitude to help one another through this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It does not mean that people who suffer from mental distress will not recover.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Given the right support, the right care environment, there is every chance that we can help one another go through the dark valleys of life.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank the hon Minister for his personal leadership in handling this tough incident.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I know that I speak for a number of hon Members of Parliament as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He can be assured that he has our full support in his endeavour to make River Valley High School emerge stronger and the rest of the school system stronger as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As the Minister mentioned, already, certain subjects or certain programmes in schools are geared towards this.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: He had also shared that if he were to just target those students who are susceptible to mental issues, there would be an issue of stigma, they may not come forward.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: So, why do we not put mental resilience as a strategic objective in school and ensure that our children, when they emerge from the education system, are mentally resilient to deal with the challenges of the future?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This will resonate throughout because when they enter the workforce, they will be mentally resilient; when they become parents, they will be mentally resilient; and so on.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, perhaps this is even more important than ever before.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have described the kind of new challenges that our young people have to go through growing up nowadays.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The world will become more uncertain, more turbulent.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Success in the future will not just depend on our technical competencies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Success in the future will very much also depend on the resilience of our people as individuals and as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why we fully agree with Mr Murali Pillai.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is the reason why we want to balance our curriculum.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will find ways to do this, notwithstanding COVID-19, because the school is not just about academic pursuits.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: School is about the holistic development of our children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We definitely want to do more for our students in this turbulent world and we thank Mr Murali Pillai for his support.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to express my sadness over the incident.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number one: preliminary investigations revealed that the 16-year-old was already assessed at IMH before.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: What is MOE's strategy with suicide prevention and post-self-harm and suicide attempts for students?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Number two: what is MOE doing to raise awareness in not just teachers but students as well?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Because such a shock could easily render a student and teacher helpless and not knowing that he or she actually needs help.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: One last question: should there be students or teachers who are deeply affected by the incident but are afraid to seek the counselling services that MOE has set in place due to entrenched stigma, what are the alternative platforms they might be able to turn to and are they actually aware of these?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Only in the exceptional cases where there is a real threat, the agencies might then take actions to work with other agencies to pre-empt this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If somebody steps forward and seeks help, we will keep the information in confidence.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But if somebody, in the process of seeking help, exhibits behaviour or expresses an intention to harm somebody else in a certain context, then the agency has a responsibility to verify and see if further actions are required to safeguard the well-being of the distressed individual and the well-being of the community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is okay to seek help early and there is no stigmatisation to seeking help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We should not, in our own behaviour, in any way, ostracise or stigmatise people who come forward and seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the third point, we are very aware and I am very concerned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not just that some young people do not know how to seek help or where to seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have also come across cases whereby parents are unsure how to seek help and where to seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why it requires us as a community to reach out to students, to youths, to families in distress to encourage them to seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it need not go through the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But the important point is to help the distressed individual or family, to point them in the right direction so that they have the confidence that they are not alone.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, I would like to ask the House and our people to avoid knee-jerk reactions, but allow the death of this precious young life to be a beacon of light for us to ask the right questions and the deeper questions to seek the answers on what is needed to protect and nurture the mental health of our people.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: To that purpose, I ask the Minister how are we strengthening our mental health discovery and support measures?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Does this currently involve a systematic way of tracking incidents across the system to shed light on the current condition of our youths' mental health and what may have led up to its current condition?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Member Ms Carrie Tan has raised very important and valid points.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The mental wellness of our society is something that we must take seriously, both at the individual level and at the community level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the individual level, for the children who are still in school, we have a system to watch over them, to understand their challenges and to provide them with the support.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But as Ms Carrie Tan suggested, we need to do more on two fronts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One, how do we systematically help a distressed individual over time?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why, in some schools, when the distressed individual has been identified, we assign dedicated teachers to help the individual, even though the teacher may no longer be the form teacher of the class.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because one of the key things about individuals seeking help is that it requires trust for a distressed individual to open up, to share with someone they can trust.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The trust required to help someone in distress requires time to build up.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why I am encouraged by the actions of many of our teachers who take it upon themselves to monitor and help students even when the students are no longer under their direct charge.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is this very intricate trust relationship that allows our students to open up with their problems.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because it is not always that our children feel comfortable opening up to even their family members.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sometimes, they need someone else and we are here to provide them with that additional channel.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the other hand, we are also concerned with the younger people who have left the school system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They do not necessarily have the same formal structure of support that we are able to provide in the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is where, as a community, we must also find ways to reach out to these distressed individuals and let them know that, even beyond the school system, there is help and there are resources available in the community to help individuals and families in distress.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not easy to pick out someone who is in distress but may not be prepared to open up.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It takes a certain depth of relationship to understand the individual, to know that something is wrong and then be able to gain the trust of the individual to seek help and go for professional help, if need be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are things that, I think, we need to do better as a community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It goes beyond individuals, it goes beyond agencies, but it does require all of us to be extra vigilant to distressed individuals who might be among us.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The first is how are we going to address the stigmatisation that may occur, that mental health issues do not equate to a propensity for violence, particularly given what has just happened?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: How do we make sure that these messages and these erroneous messages do not end up being propagated and what sort of attention is being paid to this?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I just wanted to know how is the waitlist being managed?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The distress can be expressed in various forms.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It could be expressed in being withdrawn, it could be expressed in self-harm and, perhaps, in extremis, and only in extremis, it expresses itself in harming others.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I think we all can help to spread this message.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For example, I have explained the support structure in the school and, that is, in a sense, a way for us to triage the needs of the students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the more fundamental level, perhaps the teachers or the teacher-counsellors will be adequate.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At a different level of help required, then, we have the school counsellors and the professional counsellors beyond the school system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, many of the staff who responded to the incident, they might require some assistance.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue to provide the necessary assistance for them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But Ms He Ting Ru also raised this point that perhaps all of us can also do our part to support our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All of us, as parents, we can do our part to support our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Bearing in mind, as what has been shared, that the load on today's teachers has heightened, because of the need to take care of many other matters, including the emotional well-being of our children beyond their academics.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As parents, let us work together with our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Find ways that we can support our teachers as well, in peacetime and in crisis.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us work through the Parent Support Group, so that the Parent Support Group not only supports the school, but also supports one another and be an added avenue for parents or children who require additional help, to have an additional channel of support.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister if this particular tragedy and also those students who have come forward to seek help or counselling, could it also be related to bullying?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: And what is MOE doing to address these cases of bullying, as well as cyber bullying in schools?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, the 13-year-old and the 16-year-old did not know each other prior.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It does not suggest that bullying was the cause of this particular incident.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having said that, we recognise that, in today's environment, be it physical bullying, or cyber bullying, it is an issue that we must grapple with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But we are also cognisant that, in today's society, perhaps the cyber bullying is an even greater challenge compared to the physical bullying, because this takes place away from what most of us can see around us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It takes place in the cyberspace; it takes place in the social media that our teenagers and children are exposed to.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I think we need to do two things as a society to manage this challenge.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the one hand, we need to send a clear message to the perpetrators of the bullying, be it physical or cyber, that this is not what our society stands for, that bullying is actually a sign of weakness, that you are not confident of yourself, that you have to try and tear down someone.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is not what we stand for in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is not what we will tolerate in Singapore, that all of us, as adults, have the opportunity and responsibility to amplify the positivity, both in the physical world and in the cyber domain, to be good role models to our younger generation; that be it in our choice of words or actions, that we seek to edify, we seek to build, rather than to seek to destroy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I am sure Members will agree with me the cyber bullying issue is causing distress, not just only to our young.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Even adults, grown-ups, suffer from the consequences of such actions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It could be unkind words on the social media, it could be the incessant and unrelenting comparison to make someone feel, perhaps, less adequate.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are all actions that tear down rather than build up.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have a collective responsibility and we all have the agency to do something about this as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the other hand, we need to better equip our younger generation to deal with this, to manage this, because it may not go away anytime soon.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is why we need to build the confidence in our people, in our young, especially, that they can be confident in themselves, that they can accept themselves as who they are.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They do not need to seek affirmation from their social media feeds or feel that they must be pressurised to only show that perfect image of themselves, as if the whole world is perfect, except us.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That would be a very sad state of affairs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, I always remind the students that I meet that the only reason why those posts are on the social media feed is because they are not the norm.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: People post when they find something that is out of the norm.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The artificial image that everything is perfect in the social media world is unreal.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Most of us wake up every day feeling average.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Most of us, definitely for me, we all look average.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there is no need for us to feel that we must live up to somebody else's image and be held ransom by such a psychology.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is what we need to equip our people with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For the rest who have seen their friends or other people around them being cyber bullied, we all have a right, a responsibility, to stand up for one another so that we are not torn apart, one by one.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is a new challenge for a new generation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must learn to come together, support one another, nurture one another, build up one another, not to tear down other people just to make ourselves feel relatively superior.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: No, that, itself, is a sign of weakness of the perpetrator, of the bully.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I observed that some of them were in tears and worrying that they might disappoint their parents as a result of the less desirable results that they may get from their final-year examinations.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This incident, as well as the incident at SJI, has thrown the spotlight on the importance of mental health.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I echo Mr Patrick Tay's call, which the Minister did not specifically address, and urge the Minister to consider implementing measures to regularly and systematically monitor the mental well-being of our students, like how we monitor their academic achievements and physical fitness.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This can be in the form of questionnaires that measure stress level, anxiety and depression.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I understand from mental health professionals that such questionnaires are already available.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The outcome of these questionnaires will allow us to proactively reach out to students who need help.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Without measurement, we act and react with a blindfold.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question that I have is based on earlier exchanges.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is recognition that the workload on our teachers is heavy.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such being the case, why is the enrolment at NIE dropping?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It may not be through the survey that she mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will certainly take a look at the kind of surveys possible.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I want to highlight one point from what we understand.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not just measurement alone that we should be concerned with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What is perhaps even more important is to build that trust, that relationship, that allows, encourages and not impede our people seeking help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, we will continue to recruit teachers based on the cohort requirement.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The NIE numbers do not reflect the overall support structure that we are putting in place to execute the various operations in the schools, including the teaching and the social-emotional health monitoring of our students.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In my Meet-the-People sessions (MPS), I do encounter a few cases of requests or school transfers where parents, who have children studying in the so-called more competitive schools, find their child unable to cope with the pressures or unable to fit into the school environment.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, their child's emotional well-being, the learning developments are all affected.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Minister if MOE can be more sympathetic to such requests to facilitate transfers?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I know there will be some administrative arrangements, the matching of the request to the places in the schools and there is also a transition programme needed.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But the change of environment could be what the child needs to reset and to start afresh.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The well-being of the child is our foremost consideration in enabling parents to help their child find a more suitable environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Which then comes to the second point I want to make and this is key.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think all of us, in our MPS, would have come across parents who desire their children to go to a certain school: sometimes, a school nearby for logistic reasons; sometimes, a school that is deemed to be more popular.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I always have this advice and suggestion for the parents who appeal for their children to go to some school, sometimes quite far away, but perhaps deemed to be a more popular school, and my suggestion is this: in choosing a school for our children, we must all try to start from the perspective of the child.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our job as parents is to help our children realise their potential; for them to go to an environment where they can feel confident and comfortable developing their potential, finding their footing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it is always very sad, very sad, to see a child come home from school without any sparkle in the eye, that they are just being made to feel that they are living up to someone else's expectations on them and it destroys the confidence of the child.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, it is important for us all to remember that the best gifts that we can give to our children is to help them understand their strengths and weaknesses, be confident, be comfortable with who they are, as they find their footing in this uncertain world.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not to live up to the expectations of someone else or it is not to be constantly measured according to someone else's yardstick.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We all want to nudge our children, we all want to stretch them a bit, as part of their development process and there is nothing wrong with that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But we all need to be careful that we do not inadvertently erode the confidence of the child or, worse, to destroy the sense of curiosity and desire to learn in a child because they are not in an environment that they are comfortable with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some perform well in a competitive environment, others perform well in a more nurturing environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it is best for us to start from the basis of our child's interest first.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Yes, I thank the Members for their interest in this important topic.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I hope to close the debate at 2.45 pm.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask if the school counsellor is a dedicated resource or also an educator with teaching responsibilities?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Second, can schools schedule all students to have a short meeting with the school counsellor at least once?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This will dispel the mystery and stigma of seeing a counsellor and will be similar to how all students are scheduled to see the school dentist regularly.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can the Minister confirm that all classrooms can be locked from the inside and students, including very young Primary school students, are taught how to do so?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This is so that attackers will not be able to easily enter classrooms where students are hiding.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Teacher-counsellors are teachers with teaching responsibilities but we reduce the teaching load on the teachers so that we can have them take on some counselling responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We want to reach a deployment of 1,000, which means we would have to train much more than 1,000 in order to deploy 1,000 teacher-counsellors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the second clarification, at this point in time, we are in the process of updating the security infrastructure for all of our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A lot of them are done in tandem with school renovation under the PRIME programme.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For those schools that have yet to have this type of doors installed, the teachers and the students are also taught the drill to barricade themselves, working with what they have at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I think the Minister's Statement was very reassuring in terms of the number of counsellors and the number of students that have come forward.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I lived through a somewhat similar incident in school almost two and a half decades ago.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: My best friend took his own life and, until today, for all of us who were in the class, we do not know what happened.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: All that happened was we received a phone call that morning; we came to school; our form teacher spoke to us; we went to the wake; we went home; and that was it.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Quite a number of us were affected for a long period of time.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, I am very heartened that the Minister has shared the numbers and the experience for this particular incident.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I understand that there are currently about 700 school counsellors, teacher-counsellors and we hope to deploy 1,000 in the next few years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Minister share with the House how the teachers are equipped in terms of their skillsets to identify and, perhaps, to refer students to more highly trained professionals?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second clarification has to do with this impression that when you talk about education in Singapore, the word "stress" accompanies it at all levels.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the last few weeks, parents were stressed because they were applying for school admissions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: That process has evolved over the years, but as you listen to parents, you find that stress still comes up very often.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: When I talk to my peers as well as to residents, their comments are often also about stress in school.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I always recall one of my earliest bosses saying that stress is good because it tells you that you are alive.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But more often than not, I think we are in a society where we tend to ignore somewhat the pressures of stress and how it builds up over time.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Because it is so much related to our education system, would the Minister be able to share how he thinks our education landscape should evolve over the years so that this idea of a very stressful and pressurising environment would become less so and we would have a more resilient student population and a more resilient society in the years ahead?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our current system of equipping our teachers comprises the following levels.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, this is the baseline emotional well-being literacy that we seek to share with all our teachers, so that we have a baseline to work with.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, if you can imagine, instead of teaching two subjects, they may reduce the load on teaching two subjects or reduce to even one subject but they take on additional responsibilities within the school to help in the counselling services provided by the school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, that is the next level of training for our teachers, where they will have greater depth of training in how they can intervene to help students in distress.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: School counsellors, as explained, do not have teaching responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If you like, the equivalent of this is the orientation officer in Basic Military Training (BMT) where his job is to make sure that people settle in well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are two ways which we can try to recruit full-time counsellors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One, as part of the wider community of people who are interested in full-time counselling.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These could be fresh entrants, fresh graduates, or these could be mid-career people who want to do a career switch.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is what we consider from the external system to reinforce the school counselling community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are also occasions whereby some educators, having been in the system for a while, decide to dedicate time to do full-time counselling.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is where we will re-role them into full-time school counselling duties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, this is how we build up the community of support.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If I may move on to the second issue of stress, yes, we agree with Mr Alex Yam that, in any system, there will be some amount of stress.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Too little, it does not stretch our people sufficiently.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Where is the optimal point is a careful calibration that we must do judiciously and study consciously in every step as we evolve our education system.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But how to reduce stress at the aggregate?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will be saying more of this to the school community in this year's workplan seminar, but I just want to raise two points for consideration, for all of us, so that we can perhaps think about this and, in our own way, help to carry this message.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The first is this: the definition of success.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is already hard enough for our young people to try to excel and do better than what they had done yesterday.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That constant striving for excellence, in itself, is a positive stress for them to aspire to achieve more.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second dimension which we believe in MOE and which I hope to share from my previous experience in NTUC and MTI with the school communities, is this: remember that we have a broad definition of success.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: People do well in life across many dimensions and we all do not have to go after the same yardstick.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We all can strike out in our own ways, contributing in different capacities to the development of our nation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They also very often have their people going on what they call a "gap year" or some "gap months" after their National Service for both boys and girls before they perhaps enter universities or go on to work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One Israeli told me that they have a very common question that they would ask amongst themselves: what do they do during the gap year or gap months?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not where my friends have been to and, therefore, I want to go.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They ask this question: where have my friends not been to?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I will want to go and explore the place and bring back something different for my country and my society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This struck me and left a deep impression on me because it tells me that this nation is not all going after the same definition of success.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They all believe in that diversity of ideas that can come from all around the world, that they would travel to different parts of the world to try to learn something new, something different, something that will enrich their society, something that will allow them to distinguish themselves, something that will allow them to cross-pollinate ideas and create new ideas.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I thought if all of us can take a leaf from this, we will be a much more resilient society with diverse capabilities and perhaps much less stress in all trying to pursue the same objective.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Those are my two humble suggestions for consideration.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a parent of two young children – my son is 13 years old – my heart broke when I heard the news on Monday.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, my sincere condolences to the families who have been affected by this.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do not think we can say that we understand how you feel because we do not; but our prayers and thoughts are with you during this difficult moment.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have been an educator for 20 years and, very early on in my education career, one of my students passed on.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When that happens to you, you have a troubled young man and his challenges, it is not something you forget very easily and, for a while, you are stuck between the two torments of "if only" and "what if".

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because, as we have heard, our educators are very much more than just imparters of knowledge.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They are caregivers, they are sometimes surrogate parents, they are older brothers, they are uncles, aunts and so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, I would like to just tell all our educators right now, especially those who are affected by this incident, thank you for all the good work that you have done and that you, no doubt, will continue to do and we all stand in solidarity with you.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When this incident first happened, I think many people were asking the questions: how did it happen, how could it have happened?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We heard the matter being debated and clarified quite extensively.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think the message the Minister was giving was that everybody has to work together collectively in this.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would appreciate if the Minister could provide some guidance in that area.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Darryl David's final question is a very important one.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How do we minimise the chance of this ever happening again?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And perhaps, we should start on the premise that this can happen again, but the chances of this happening again will be much diminished if we all come together to support one another.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We can all come together as a community to spread the message that we should not stigmatise anyone who is in distress.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That it takes courage for people to come forward to seek help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That we will not ostracise them and we will still accept them as who they are.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It takes all of us to look out for one another to prevent this tragedy from ever happening again.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the individual level, at the school level, at the family level, at the community level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It takes all of us to build that caring and nurturing environment that seeks to build up our people rather than to tear them down.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is our responsibility as adults to lend our shoulders to the next generation to stand taller, see further and have greater confidence to pursue their dreams in their own ways.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When I first arrived in the school, Mrs Teo, the Principal, received me.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: She was in pain, not just physically but emotionally.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They were also in pain and in shock.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But none of them thought about their own pain, shock or grief.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They were all busy running around, making sure that each and every child under their charge was well taken care of first.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They did not even have time to think about themselves nor grieve.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And the final incident that I would like to share with this House.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I spoke with some of the students while they were waiting to be interviewed by the Police.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some of them were the classmates of the 16-year-old.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Amidst their pain and their confusion as to what had happened, how it could have happened, two of them told me the same thing, separately.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They just had one simple request for me.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They told me, "Minister, please help our friend, the 16-year-old.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Please take care of him." They know it is a cry for help.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The way they carried themselves, the way they responded to the incident, will be etched in my mind forever.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And it is they who will inspire us to do all we can for the next generation, for the distressed members amongst us in our community, regardless of age.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That we will do our utmost so that this incident will never be repeated.

speaker: Deputy Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
